exposure: polygenic scores for psychiatric and neurodevelopmental conditions
cohort: The cohort consists of 7859 women from the Norwegian Mother, Father, and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) with clinically significant postpartum depression, whose first recorded pregnancies were between 1999 and 2008.
finding: The study identified and validated seven reproducible postpartum depression (PPD) subtypes, which were differentiated by symptom severity, onset timing, trauma history, pain during pregnancy, and showed distinct genetic and obstetric profiles.
mod_finding: One early-onset PPD subtype characterized by pain had a higher prevalence of birth by caesarean section (10% in the training set and 8% in the test set).
